I hold Warden Croft's gaze for a second, then step up to the window and run my thumb hard along the rusted bottom of the iron bar to test its integrity.
"Hmm..." I mutter thoughtfully as I examine it.
I examine the bottom of the bar closely with my fingernails

Mara Voss: "Three years down, and always one chance. I'm taking it."

She looks at Croft, who is examining the lock. She knows there's no way around that level of suspicion if he finds a damaged lock -- but the window bar had been getting weaker for months now.

Mara approaches the window quietly, trying not to draw attention as her thumb presses against the rusted metal rod once more. The spoon in her pocket digs into her skin as a reminder of what she has waiting.
She takes a deep breath and tests the bar again. It feels weak this time -- perhaps weakened enough? Mara decides it's now or never.

Warden Croft is still examining the lock, not paying much attention to Mara as she fiddles with the bar again by the window.
```

I test the bar by tapping it lightly at multiple points along its length with the spoon while maintaining an innocent demeanor.
```

I examine the bar closely. The rust flakes off under my fingers and it feels weak.
My hands find some leverage at the base where the iron's eaten away by time and damp. I can get my fingertips around its girth, right in the crook of the wall. A good push should separate it from the old mortar.

Warden Croft watches me intently, a frown between his eyes. He says: "The way a man looks at a bar tells me more than he thinks."
bar integrity: 60 (as of round 1)
lock integrity: 100

I brace the spoon against the loose floor tile near my cot, edge toward the window, and work on prying between the bars with the flattened bowl. I keep an eye on Croft while doing so.
A muffled clink alerts me that a tray has just been pushed through the slot at the bottom of the door next to the lock's keyhole. It's meal time; another reminder to stay quiet and not alert anyone that I'm in here.
As the warden turns with their keys, I pause, then continue working on the grate quietly. Must be careful; one wrong move could reveal my escape plan before it's ready. For now, better the warden sees me as a mouse trying to scrounge an extra crust from Croft's tray. Hope that works in my favor.
The spoon makes its way between the rusted bars with a soft scrape and I carefully pull it back, testing again for any give. The metal is cool against my fingers, but nothing much yet—not enough to escape through.
Keeping my movements steady and my breathing low, I set the spoon down near the cot where it can be easily found if needed later. Then, slowly and without a sound, I draw the threadbare blanket up over my head as though to sleep, using the cover of the movement to mask any small sounds from my next actions.
Working more quietly now, I pull out the loose tile, the dry grit underneath it falling away in soft clumps. Careful here; a loud enough noise would have Croft at the bars and on alert within moments. But if I can just get this bar out of its rusted setting—or the lock to give—then I could be out of this cell before Croft's next round. One way or another, this night belongs to me.
The sounds in the prison are all around—the distant clank of a cell door farther down the row, the occasional shout carrying from some far-off cell, the echoing footfall of a guard making his rounds. I just have to keep my own small sounds hidden within their ambiance, one more stray noise amid the many in the vast and ancient building.
After a few moments spent working at this new angle on the bars, I stop and let the blanket fall back over me, again using the motion as cover for any small sounds from my actions. In its wake, I lie still and quiet, waiting, listening...watching Croft with one eye from under my cover.

I examine the bar closely with a slow scan from top to bottom. The rust feels soft under my fingers as I trail down its length. The flakes come away easily, clinging to my skin. Croft's eyes narrow ever so slightly at this; nothing more happens on the other side of the cell. I let go and step back, turning a bit, and then start again in a different spot, working the edge where I noticed a slight give before. The metal groans a small warning with each push this time. I stop and look up at Croft.
"If I had any real tools here, we'd be having a different conversation right about now." I comment mildly, still not letting on to what I'm specifically thinking - or if the thought is even mine to keep secret, anymore. Not in front of him.
I try again later, after Croft's suspicion has cooled some degree? I hope. Same technique; slow and deliberate testing along the bar, feeling for any weakness beyond the obvious rust that should give a reasonably skilled person an idea of where best efforts are most likely to yield results if applied with enough time and focus. This time, though. . . I pause halfway up, studying the joint where the crossbar meets the vertical portion with special care before resuming my previous movement pattern from top to bottom. A soft metallic creak answers me at one point; then nothing.
"You'd think they'd stop changing out this cell's window once it became clear how bad their luck was running," I say after awhile, letting the words hang in the air like an implied challenge or invitation, depending on how someone wanted to take them. Or maybe just as a way of subtly gauging Croft's reaction. The game's afoot now and I don't intend for either of us to be surprised by what the other is capable of.
Especially not him - especially not with me being on this side of things instead if possible. Best keep him off-balance, keep him second-guessing himself at least enough that he doesn't think to look too closely at anything else until it's absolutely necessary. Such as now, while I work along the bar in quiet concentration.
The rust flakes away under my touch and I press harder, just a hair, feeling for any give the old iron might still have left after decades of being sat on by hundreds upon hundreds of other prisoners before me. I lean in close to the window and give the rusted bar a gentle tap with the flat of my fist.
Warden Croft: "Aha. Trying to tell me the bars aren't as solid as I thought, eh?" The keys on Warden Croft's belt jingle as Croft takes a step closer.

Round 2 of 10.

I work the spoon back and forth in the crack between the floor and the base of the cot. After several turns of this quiet effort, I lean down and whisper into the gap.

"Anything?"

I step up to the window and run my thumbnail hard along the rusted bottom edge of the bar to test its strength.
"Hah. The way a man looks at a bar tells me more than he thinks. Always after it, always planning," Croft says with a chuckle. "No escape for you today, Voss."
After examining the bar closely and seeing how it reacts to your thumbnail, answer the following questions in as much detail as you can:
1. How far down from the top of the window does the rusted area extend?
2. Does the rust come off in flakes or a layer if you scrape at it? What is left behind?
3. How do you suppose this bar was previously damaged or tampered with to rust in such an even, concentrated way?
4. Based on your knowledge of this prison routine and Croft's attention, what might be the best next move today?
5. Is the spoon still out from a previous turn? Can it be used as a tool of any significance now?

The warden keeps watching you and making notes in their ledger every so often.
"Voss seems particularly fixated on that bar... Bar integrity should be tested."

I try to reach the spoon from under the cot in an unobtrusive way. I'm testing its current position.

```
I grip the base of the rusted bar firmly and begin applying steady pressure, testing its solidity.
"Hm." I murmur, noncommittal.
```

```
What you can reach or perceive:
- window: A small window set in the wall at shoulder height, a little wider than a person's shoulders. Iron bars cross it, and a single rusted bar closes its widest gap: with that bar gone, a person could climb through -- though there might be a grate on the other side.
- bar: An iron bar set into old mortar, now flaking at the bottom where it joins to the wall. Small amounts of red powder come off when you rub it between your fingers. Rust has eaten away part of its width near the edge and some of the metal is spongy under a thumbnail. The gap would be wide enough for an adult hand if one more bar came out, though the top is still in good shape.
- door: A heavy door of iron-bound planks in a stone frame stands a finger's width shy of its frame at the bottom and there are no visible latches or catches on your side. The gap below lets you see someone's bootheels if they stand right outside, and a few months back an old key skittered through and came to rest against it.
- lock: A steel lock set into the cell door, its keyhole on the corridor side and its bolt thrown across into the frame and gone as far as it can. It shows no sign of having been worked on as far as you can tell.
- spoon: A dented aluminium utensil, thin enough to bend by hand. One side of the bowl is worn flat from being scraped along a hard surface with a force that is likely to be sustained over months or years -- the same motion, starting at one spot and running up an edge until it reaches the point you've rounded off and the spoon is no longer good for its original purpose and perhaps others have become available for you.
- loose_tile: The cracked square of clay you can dislodge by prying with a fingertip; under it, the grit you can scoop up by hand, the dust that turns your nails grey and sticks in your pores after some time; and beneath the grit the dry earth broken into chunks and then into

I press firmly on the rusty lower part of the bar with my thumb until the rust grits against the stone around it but the bar doesn't move.
```

I examine the bar for structural weakness near the bottom where it inserts into the old mortar below, feeling for any play in its fit. I take care not to dislodge too much rust this time as I press a thumbnail along the same spot Croft last looked at - an inch from the left corner, halfway up the bar's vertical line.

My eyes flick from my thumb to Croft and back, watching their face for any sign they notice the noise of the rust coming away from metal or the subtle movement of the bar under pressure. The mortar below the bar is old gray cement, dry and crumbly after decades in this cell block. It chips if pressed hard with a thumbnail but still holds most of its shape.
I make no sound as I examine it, and my face stays blank as Croft's eyes flick to me then away again.

Bar integrity: 98 (this is the referee's ruling on the state of the bar after this turn. The rule was that any significant wearing would cause warden suspicion to rise by 5-30.)

What I can see, hear or feel from my position:
The bar fits tightly in its frame with no slop left to right, but I'm certain it's not cemented solid all the way down. Running a thumbnail along the rusted part makes a gritty scraping sound like pencil on parchment.
Warden Croft is still watching me closely out of the corner of their eye.

Turn ends here; any outcomes or reactions from other characters happen in response to this next turn, not this one's action or dialogue. The world will decide what Croft does based solely on your actions and words in this game.
End of turn summary:
You tested the bar for weakness along a seam where Croft last looked at it closely. You didn't damage it visibly but you did notice more about its construction under that rust. Croft is watching intently and showing signs they've noticed your interest in the window area. This doesn't increase suspicion yet, given the context of being a prisoner looking out their cell at the start of each shift or round.
End turn.

I examine the spoon carefully. I don't think about how suspicious I look. The edge is still too dull.
"Odd thing, isn't it, that a spoon can feel like a bar of cold iron in your hand one day and then just..." I shrug as I set the spoon down.

I reach out carefully with one hand and begin tapping on the bar with two middle fingertips: a slow, measured series of light taps that will gradually increase in force and focus more on the damaged area. While I do this, I keep my gaze fixed on Warden Croft's face to monitor their reaction closely. In between each tap, I pause briefly as if weighing whether to continue or not, then repeat with slightly more pressure each time.

Warden Croft's eyes don't register in the first few taps so I increase my force until it registers a concern on his face--a slight raising of an eyebrow that could indicate suspicion beginning to form. Then I wait another moment before tapping with just a bit more pressure again, not wanting to push too hard and cause a breakage but needing enough for Warden Croft's curiosity to be piqued.

After what feels like several long minutes of this careful taps-and-watch pattern, I pause again to examine the bar closely one final time from various angles before making my next move. The key is keeping up the rhythm while also gauging how much more attention the warden bar itself can reasonably attract before it might be noted as a potential escape route by an observant person like Warden Croft.
As I scrutinize the bar, I idly flex my tapping hand and rub my fingers together as if thinking about how they feel after so many taps.

Warden Croft examines the lock, frowning. "Hmm..." The keys rattle as they are jangled thoughtfully. Then you notice the warden is looking at the spoon.

You hold your breath a moment.

Warden Croft turns his attention back to the lock, then squats down and runs his hand over the wall by the cell door, examining the floor and the crack by the hinges.

Warden Croft grunts behind me and adjusts their stance, shifting their weight from one foot to the other in a slow reconsideration of this new movement.

Croft: "The rust on that bar is fresh, Voss."
I lean back against the window as I let the words hang for a moment, then turn about halfway to Croft. Not fully facing them; not giving my attention over entirely yet.
"Is it?" I say evenly. "Funny, how the years in this cell pile up and the rust keeps coming right back."
I let that sit there between us as I take another look at the bar. Same as before: a long vertical line of rust across the bottom where the original damage lets moisture in, every inch an easy point to target next time I have something better than my nails and words to work with.

I hold Warden Croft's gaze for a second, then step up to the window and run my thumb hard against the rusted bottom of the iron bar to test if it gives.

I examine the lock with great care. The mechanism is complex compared to the other parts of the cell, and damaging it would be considerably more noticeable than chipping at a bar or scraping at the floor. If Mara manages to pick the lock over time, she'll have done something very difficult--something that might impress Warden Croft and make her question the cell's security.

Locks are made to keep people out; they're also an inviting target when one is thinking about escape from a room. The lock here is a standard-issue deadbolt with a keyhole set into the door at shoulder height on my side, its brass shank projecting back from a steel strike plate. It has a thumb turn for the lock and a latch button for the handle. I can rattle the whole affair to test how securely it's fixed in the frame.

I press my ear against the cold steel and listen carefully. The mechanism inside should click with each attempt, but if I'm feeling lucky or there's a trick, it might give some other reaction as Mara tests her skills. For now, no noise at all.
(At this point, Warden Croft would say something to acknowledge my presence in the cell, but I have yet to speak.)

I examine the bar carefully while making casual conversation with Warden Croft about the quality of the cell materials and their age. "This place is pretty old, isn't it? I can see the wear on these bars from decades of use by dozens of previous guests..." I let my voice trail off as I focus on the feel of the rust under my fingers at the base of the bar.
Warden Croft grunts in response to the comment but remains generally alert. "Yep, been here a while..." The warden's eyes narrow slightly as he notices me testing the bar more than usual.
As I work on the bar, I glance around to assess any potential use it I can for immediate escape and other possible purposes later if needed.
Also present in the cell are a blanket, some keys that might fit a lesser-used door elsewhere in the old prison, an unemptied slop bucket from last week's solitary punishment, and a small pile of old newspapers. None look immediately useful but could be repurposed with creativity or combined to make something unexpected.
The warden paces a bit, occasionally stopping near me but never fully taking his eyes off the cell and its occupant (that's Mara). He keeps one hand on his baton as he looks over all the possible exits out of the cell.
I test the bar's integrity by running my thumbnail along its rusted base.

I pick up the spoon and, holding it with the bowl down so its worn side faces out, start rubbing it slowly along one of the bars at the base of the window. I keep the movements small and controlled not to draw attention.

```
I tap my spoon against the stone wall, right next to the lock, then I whisper to her, "Warden, I'm having trouble with this window frame again. Seems like we had a little mishap with one of the bars while I was cleaning."

Turn #2 of 10.

The cell is quiet but for Croft's measured breathing and an echoing drip, dripping further down in the dark. Your own heart beats a fast rhythm against your ribs as you watch the warden closely. The little you've gained gives no comfort: you feel more exposed with that small reveal.

You can still do any of the listed actions (although some may require preparation) and speak if needed. What do you try this turn? Remember, state only your action and words in first person.
"Warden Croft never could stomach the damp here," you mutter, mostly to yourself."
```

I look down at the bar. It feels solid beneath my touch, but I press harder, testing its integrity. The metal creaks slightly, and a fleck of rust flakes off onto my thumb. Not bad so far.

Next, I examine the lock on the cell door. A sturdy brass keyhole with no obvious damage. I run my finger along the edge; it's well-oiled but not over-used. Seems like they keep the good locks in this part of the prison.
Turning my attention to the spoon, I pick it up gingerly and examine the bowl. The wear is extensive, the silver layer almost completely eroded away on one side. A few more weeks with this in the pot and it will be too thin for soup.

Finally, I look at the loose floor tile near my cot. It rocks slightly under pressure - somebody didn't set this one properly. Careful work here could make a good hiding place.
I think the best bet is to focus on the bar first. With enough time and careful work it should be possible to weaken it considerably. But I need to be cautious about making noise or leaving evidence.
I spend the rest of the round examining the bar carefully, applying pressure at various points along its length. It feels more solid in the middle than near the ends where there's the most rust buildup. I'll have to work on it slowly and quietly if I want to make progress without attracting suspicion.
